newsitem.title: USA: El Paso signs San Juan gas compression deal.
newsitem.headline: El Paso signs San Juan gas compression deal.

text.p: El Paso Field Services, a unit of El Paso Energy Corp, said Tuesday it signed agreements with three major natural gas producers in the San Juan Basin, providing for new compression services to reduce field pressures and increase production in the area.

The $50 million project, signed with Burlington Resources, Amoco Production Co and Conoco Inc, includes the installation of about 36,000 horsepower of new field compression and will boost production from the San Juan area by an estimated 130 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd).
The deal also provides for an additional 56 miles of pipeline. Work is scheduled to be completed by mid-1998.

El Paso Field Services, the largest natural gas gatherer in the San Juan Basin with throughput of more than one billion cubic feet per day (bcfd), will install 10 new compressor units at five separate locations on its 5,500 mile system.
These additional units will lower average wellhead pressures to 150 pounds per square inch gauge (psig) on 70 percent of its high pressure gathering system, affecting approximately 3,000 wells.
Additionally, the majority of the increased volumes will be delivered to El Paso's Chaco Cryogenic Processing Plant which processed an average of 472 mmcfd in the first quarter of 1997.

"This project represents a cooperative effort by El Paso and its largest producers to extend the productive life of the San Juan Basin natural gas reserves through this innovative global compression service," Robert C. Phillips, president of El Paso Field Services, said in a statement.

El Paso Energy Corp provides total energy solutions through five business units: El Paso Natural Gas Company, Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company, El Paso Field Services Company, El Paso Energy Marketing Company and El Paso Energy International Company.
The company has operations in interstate natural gas transmission, gas gathering and processing, energy marketing and international energy infrastructure development.
